links.outcome: LLM accuracy across data quality levels and timeframes in interpreting phenotyping data
links.effect: GPT-4o accuracy declined with decreasing data quality (69% high-quality vs 39% low-quality) and shorter timeframes (60% for 3-month vs 43% for 3-week data).
links.quote: Accuracy declined with decreasing data quality (69% for high-quality data vs 39% for low-quality data) and shorter timeframes (60% for 3-month data vs 43% for 3-week data).

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs on the same test cases for pattern identification accuracy
links.effect: GPT-4o 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) significantly outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).
links.quote: GPT-4o demonstrated 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) in identifying clinical patterns based on standard test cases, significantly outperforming GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance (GPT-4o vs GPT-3.5) on interpreting simulated psychiatric digital phenotyping test cases without comparing or testing a deployment practice.
